The 2027 MegaLounge 540 Squeezes a Mega Lounge Inside the Tiniest Campervan
15 photos
Photo: YouTube/The Motorhome Review Channel
Tiny is what tiny does, but never underestimate what creative design, plenty of skill, and a willingness to go against the trend can do in terms of turning even the smallest campervan into a nice two-person RV you won't hate yourself for choosing. Case in point, the MegaMobil Lounge 540.
The MegaMobil Lounge 540, or the MegaLounge 540 as it's also been called, has been around for several years now, changing ever so little from one iteration to the other. That's the surest sign that Slovenian manufacturer MegaMobil hit the right spot from the start with the model.
The only thing the 2027 model year brings new is a series of additional extras. This is the smallest version of the MegaLounge compact RV that MegaMobil offers but it's just as customizable as its bigger siblings. In between the interior and exterior options and the extra packs available, you get the chance to turn your compact RV into a personalized one. It will still be small, but it will be truly yours.
The MegaLounge sits on a Stellantis chassis, whether a Peugeot Boxer or a Fiat Ducato, offered standard with a 140-hp engine and manual transmission, and a 3,500-kg (7,716-lb) maximum permissible weight.
Photo: MegaMobil Both these can be upgraded if you want to, so you can move to automatic and 180 hp, or uprate the maximum weight, in which case you do get more payload capacity but you will also need to upgrade your B Category driving license.
Whatever your choice, one thing won't change: this is one of the tiniest yet most complete campervans on the market right now. The MegaLounge 540 comes in at just 5.4 meters (17.7 feet) of total length and a width of 2.05 meters (6.07 feet), which makes it ideal for driving even in crowded or narrow city streets.
Despite its very compact dimensions, it offers sleeping for as many as four people (though it would hardly be a pleasurable experience), a full wet bathroom, a nice galley, and the Mega Lounge promised in the name itself.
Photo: MegaMobil It also comes with plenty of style and functionality , and nice touches like padded walls, soft-touch ceilings, soft-close cabinetry, and accent lighting. Another noteworthy aspect is how MegaMobil goes the extra length to build storage wherever possible. If you think about it, with an RV this compact, you'd be a fool not to make the most of every inch of space – and MegaMobil are definitely not fools.
The layout puts the bathroom behind the driver's seat, the kitchen on the campside, and that oversize, very comfortable lounge at the back, with an automatic drop-down bed on top. Everything onboard is compact, obviously, except for the lounge, which is perfect for cozy two-person meals and might even work for four.
To that end, MegaMobil builds it with nice backrests with integrated storage and an adjustable table. Another surprise here is that you can also drop the table all the way and convert the entire space into a double bed. Keeping in mind the dimensions of the campervan, sleeping four people in here is a case of "just because you can doesn't mean you should," so keep that as an emergency option.
Photo: MegaMobil The main bed, however, is overhead. It drops down at the press of a button, revealing access to overhead storage and a nice skylight.
The galley is standard, with a two-burner gas cooktop and sink combo, overhead storage, and additional cabinetry under the counter, which also includes a small extension for more prep space. In a bid to add even more functionality, MegaMobil adds another extension to the outside, as well as access to the cabinets from there.
The bathroom is another neat surprise, small as it might be.
Photo: MegaMobil It's a wet one but it works almost like a dry bathroom because MegaMobil uses a glass door that swings out and covers the space where the sink, cassette toilet, and a cabinet are, while also freeing up the washing space. When you don't need the shower, the same door swings over and covers it.
For an RV of this size, having a full bathroom is an absolute luxury – and MegaMobil delivers it.
In terms of standard equipment, the MegaLounge 540 comes in three trims (Core, Advanced, and Premium), to which you can add from a list of optional packages like Escape, Freedom, and Autonomy. The last one, as its name says, offers solar panels on the roof, a 300Ah battery pack, a 2000W inverter, an awning, and an induction cooktop in lieu of the gas variant.
Photo: MegaMobil Standard across all of them will be gas-electric Truma blown air heating, a Truma water heater, a backup camera, tinted flush-mounted windows, a MaxxAir vent fan, A TV on a bracket in the lounge, and 75 liters (20 gallons) of freshwater and 80 liters (21 gallons) of gray. Like most European RVs, regardless of size, the MegaLounge 540 comes with a cassette toilet, which means there is no black water tank onboard.
Sale prices will depend on trim, optional packages , optional colors and fabrics, and lastly, the dealer you source your unit from.
Photo: MegaMobil That said, the price for the 2027 model year starts at €72,173, which is approximately $78,500 at the current exchange rate. It's not the cheapest micro-RV out there, so you could say pricing is the only part about it that's not teeny-tiny.
Via // The Motorhome Review Channel on YouTube
